_readme: Worked behavioural cases for the data-availability classifier (issue #105).
Python, Swift (BioMedLit) and Kotlin (Android) each run every case through their
own analyzer and assert the same disclosure level and the same ordered list of
restriction labels. This is the half of the parity guard that a string comparison
of the pattern lists cannot provide: it catches regex-engine differences, missing
compile flags, and tier-ordering changes, where the patterns are spelled
`restrictions` order is significant. It is the order the patterns appear in the
restricted tier, with any effectively-unavailable signals first, deduplicated by
`why` records what a case pins, for cases whose point is not obvious from the
statement. Do not reword a statement carrying a `why`: several pin a regex window
or barrier at an exact token distance and lose their discriminating power if the

cases.why: A missing statement is NOT_STATED on every platform.
An empty statement is NOT_STATED; all three guard on emptiness, not blankness.
Whitespace is deliberately NOT treated as empty: it matches nothing and falls to UNKNOWN.
